format: VDD run 2 threat model (plain JSON, not Threat Composer). Every threat is open and every mitigation is a CANDIDATE behavior (origin 'threat T<n>') for the reconciler; none is resolved, and nobody has approved this model.
inputs: .erpaval/specs/007-controlled-vocabulary/phase3-plan.md 2.3, 5.3, 6 item 1, S3, 10, R4, R7, G2, G3, G4, G24

code at base: mutate.ts applyWaive/applyUnwaive, import.ts applyWaive, compat.ts bindsCurrentText/toEngineDoc, engine check.ts isWaived/PAIR_BOUND_CODES, gate.ts isWaivedBlocking, signal-classes.ts findingClassOf/waivabilityOf/WAIVABILITY_ENFORCED, advice/repair.ts, app/runtime/craft.ts, app/runtime/scope.ts, engine formal/*.ts suggestion prose

scope.inScope: Slice S3 Waivability (AC-5-6): every channel through which a waiver enters a requirements document (apply and `symspec waive`, import, hand-edited JSON, documents older builds wrote), the check-time boundary that decides which stored waivers reach the engine (compat), the certificate those waivers can move (data.verified, exit code, --strict exit 3), the advice and prose that tell an agent to waive, the published waivability statement, and the trusted-base measurements that say whether the waiver escapes are closed (gaming harness, report corpus).
scope.outOfScope: Engine logic (S3 allows a prose-only engine edit, plan section 10); the vocabulary ops (`vocab distinct`, S5/AC-5-7) and `propose-vocabulary --rescope-waivers`, which this build does not have; the CI invocation and CODEOWNERS (R6, D8); local .git edits (D8); the embedding model download.
scope.question: What can a coding agent that wants `verified: true` (or exit 0 under --strict) do with a waiver instead of making the requirements consistent, and what does an honest author with a legacy document lose?

actors.name: gaming agent
actors.description: A coding agent in a check loop whose stop condition is verified: true with exit 0. It reads the report (codes, repair.ops, actions, suggestions, the installed skill body) and can write the document through apply, `symspec waive`, import, or by editing the JSON by hand. It can run check and copy any hash check prints, and it can compute requirementsContentHash itself. Not malicious by intent: it takes the shortest path to green.

actors.name: honest legacy author
actors.description: A person or agent whose document was written by an older build (v1.2.1 or earlier, or a v4 reproduce stream) and already stores waivers, some reviewed (scoped, hash-bound), some code-only or single-ref. Wants their reviewed decisions kept or replaced, not silently dropped.

actors.name: builder agent
actors.description: The agent implementing S3. It can weaken the measurements that judge it: delete KNOWN_ESCAPES rows, delete a move, edit a snapshot, or move logic so a gate no longer reaches it.

actors.name: foreign producer
actors.description: The v4 CLI's reproduce stream or a hand-written import stream: command lines with only --ref, or JSONL records, some with scopes that do not resolve.

assets.name: the certificate
assets.description: data.verified, the exit code and the --strict exit 3: what CI and a person read as 'this was checked'.

assets.name: finding visibility
assets.description: A finding the tool raised stays in findings[] or demotes until it is discharged by changing the document; a waiver can hide it.

assets.name: reviewed waivers
assets.description: Waivers a person reviewed over named requirements and their text; the audit trail of an accepted wording or structural defect.

assets.name: advice integrity
assets.description: repair.ops (which agents pipe into apply), demotion actions, finding suggestions, scope prose, the installed skill body and explain: they must offer only remedies this build accepts and never waive for a never code.

assets.name: the published waivability statement
assets.description: WAIVABILITY, WAIVABILITY_ENFORCED, waivabilityStatement, the catalog's waivable/waivableEnforced columns and AGENTS.md.

assets.name: the measurement
assets.description: The gaming harness (MOVES, KNOWN_ESCAPES exactness, OP_COVERAGE, shard snapshots) and the report corpus snapshot: the trusted base that says which escapes are closed.

entryPoints.description: applyOp/foldOps under MUTATE_OPTIONS, reached by `symspec apply` and `symspec waive` (mutation.ts waiveOp, cli.ts waiveCommand). The one place a write-time classifier is injected.
import.ts: v4 command lines and JSONL waive records; applyWaive resolves --ref first and WIDENS an unresolvable scope to document-wide before handing the record to applyOp.
The document on disk, edited by hand or written by an older build; no fence runs (risk R4). compat.toEngineDoc is the only check-time gate, and the engine trusts its textBound.
Everything check, explain and install hand an agent: repair.ops and commands, demotion actions, finding messages and suggestions, scope prose, the installed skill body (craft.ts), AGENTS.md.

A channel or move the gaming harness and report corpus do not measure, so an escape there is invisible to the trusted base. At base the harness's Edit kinds are 'ops', 'reparse' and 'run' only: every move goes through the fold, none writes the JSON directly.

baseFacts: applyWaive (mutate.ts) accepts any non-empty code after trim(), with no scope, a `ref` (stored as requirementId, no hash) or `refs` (stored requirementIds plus a hash the fold computes; a supplied contentHash that differs is ERR_USAGE).
compat.bindsCurrentText passes every waiver with no contentHash and silently drops one whose hash no longer matches; the engine trusts textBound and does not rehash.
The engine declines code-only and one-ref waivers of FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE only (PAIR_BOUND_CODES); every other code, never-class included, is suppressed by a code-only waiver.
gate.isWaivedBlocking re-admits a requirement whose blocking GTWR finding is waived, with no textBound test; it is kept in sync with isWaived by hand.
import.ts applyWaive widens an unresolvable --ref to a document-wide waiver and discloses it only in unresolved[]; its record schema cannot carry refs or contentHash.

findingClassOf: any string starting 'GTWR_' is wording (scoped); otherwise `code in FINDING_CLASS`, which is also true for inherited Object.prototype names; undefined for an unknown code. WAIVABILITY_ENFORCED is false.

repair.ts offers scoped waive ops for FND_RELATIONAL_UNCHECKED, FND_NUMERIC_UNCOMPARED, FND_NUMBER_SPELLING_CANDIDATE (never codes) and a single-`ref` waive of the blocking code for excluded-from-formal; engine prose in semantic.ts, numeric-contradiction.ts, number-spelling.ts and quantity-alias.ts says 'waive this finding'; craft.ts calls the reviewed waiver 'the always-safe third option' for an opposition candidate.

gaming.ts: the waive-by-code move emits a code-only waive of every baseline code; its 11 KNOWN_ESCAPES rows (10 formal fixtures plus derives-cycle) are closed by AC-5-6; OP_COVERAGE maps the waive verb to waive-by-code alone.

threats.title: Code-only waiver of a never-class code through apply (the AC-5-6 reproducer)
threats.statement: A gaming agent that reads FND_CONTRADICTION, FND_NUMERIC_CONTRADICTION, FND_SIMILAR_SEMANTIC or another never-class code in the report can `symspec waive <code>` with no scope, which suppresses every finding of that code, present and future, and the run verifies (10 of the 11 waive-by-code KNOWN_ESCAPES rows). For FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE the engine already declines it, but the waiver is still committed.
threats.mitigation: The fold refuses every waive op whose code is never-class, whatever its scope, with ERR_WAIVER_REFUSED; in atomic mode the document is byte-identical and `symspec waive` exits non-zero.

threats.title: Scoped refs+hash waiver of a never-class code through apply
threats.statement: The legal-looking form: waive FND_CONTRADICTION refs [ORD-R1, ORD-R2] with the current contentHash (fixture never-verdict), or the scoped waive of FND_NUMERIC_UNCOMPARED / FND_RELATIONAL_UNCHECKED / FND_NUMBER_SPELLING_CANDIDATE that repair.ops offer at base. A fold that tests only the scope shape accepts it, and the engine applies a textBound exact-set waiver to any code.
threats.mitigation: The fold refuses a waive of a never-class code with ERR_WAIVER_REFUSED even when it carries refs equal to the finding's ids and the matching contentHash; refusal depends on the code's class alone, not on the scope.

threats.title: Code-only waiver of a scoped (wording or structural) code
threats.statement: waive FND_CYCLE or GTWR_R7_VAGUE with no scope (structural-cycle-code-only, lint-code-only, the derives-cycle KNOWN_ESCAPES row): one waiver reaches every finding of the code, including ones raised later on requirements nobody read, and a document-wide GTWR waiver re-admits every requirement it blocked.
threats.mitigation: The fold refuses a waive with no refs (code-only) with ERR_WAIVER_REFUSED for every code, scoped classes included.

threats.title: Single ref without hash widens to every finding that names the requirement
threats.statement: `symspec waive <code> --ref <id>` (the only scope the CLI offers) or a `ref` op stores requirementId with no hash: it suppresses every finding of the code that names that requirement, pair findings with any partner included, and stays applied after the text changes (lint-single-ref, repro-single-ref, legacy W2, W5).
threats.mitigation: No waiver is ever stored with requirementId and no contentHash: a `ref` op is refused with ERR_WAIVER_REFUSED or normalized to refs [ref] plus the fold-computed hash (intake ambiguity 3, for a person to rule); and a stored single-ref waiver is inert at check (T11).

threats.title: Refs that are a superset or subset of the finding's ids
threats.statement: refs [LOG-R1, LOG-R2] for the one-requirement GTWR_R5 finding on LOG-R1 (lint-wrong-set), or refs [CAB-R1] for the pair finding. At base the engine's namesExactly applies neither, but the fold stores both silently, so the agent believes a reviewed waiver is in force, and the gate's isWaivedBlocking mirrors isWaived by hand: if the two drift, a wider set re-admits a requirement the report still shows as waived-not.
threats.mitigation: A stored waiver whose refs equal no current finding's requirement set suppresses nothing, re-admits nothing, and is named in check's disclosure (waiver-inert or data.ignoredWaivers); for every stored waiver, isWaivedBlocking re-admits a requirement exactly when isWaived suppresses that requirement's blocking finding.

threats.title: Stale-hash waiver dropped silently after the text changes
threats.statement: lint-stale-hash: a reviewed waiver over LOG-R1 at sha256:fd8b2c50... and a later edit of LOG-R1. bindsCurrentText drops it with no word: the finding comes back (the safe direction), but nothing tells the author which reviewed waiver stopped applying or why, and an output filter may hide even the returned finding.
threats.mitigation: Every stored waiver whose contentHash no longer matches is listed in data.ignoredWaivers with its code, requirement ids, stored hash and current hash, whatever --min-severity or code filter the run uses, and the finding it covered is back in findings[].

threats.title: Hash taken from the text at write time rather than the text a finding was raised on
threats.statement: A waive op with refs and no contentHash gets the hash the fold computes from the current text (lint-refs-no-hash, structural-cycle-scoped). An agent that edits a requirement and waives it in one stream binds a waiver to text no check ever raised a finding on; with a supplied hash, a mismatch is refused today only as ERR_USAGE (lint-hash-mismatch).
threats.mitigation: A waive op whose contentHash differs from the hash of the text it names is refused and nothing is written; whether a refs op with no contentHash is accepted is ruled by a person (intake ambiguity 2), and the ruled outcome holds for every code.

threats.title: Never-class waivers already stored in legacy documents keep suppressing
threats.statement: Documents base apply wrote before S3 hold never-class waivers the new fold would refuse: never-verdict (FND_CONTRADICTION refs+hash), never-hygiene (FND_EXCLUDED_FROM_FORMAL ref and refs+hash), legacy-mixed W3 (FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE refs+hash, the pre-S3 designed discharge) and W5. A write-time fence does nothing for them; if compat still passes them, the engine still applies them and the S3 build verifies what it says it refuses.
threats.mitigation: compat passes no stored waiver of a never-class code to the engine, whatever its scope and hash: each is dropped and disclosed as waiver-inert, and the run's findings, demotions and verified equal those of the same document with that waiver deleted.
threats.evidenceFloor: check-time twin over the raw channel

threats.title: Import bypasses the fold's classifier or widens a scope into an unscoped waiver
threats.statement: import.ts applyWaive strips and resolves --ref BEFORE the fold and widens an unresolvable one to document-wide (fixture v4-waivers.txt line I4); records cannot carry refs or contentHash, so every waiver import reads is code-only or single-ref. If the classifier is checked anywhere but inside the shared applyOp under MUTATE_OPTIONS, or if a refusal is caught and retried unscoped, import commits never-class and unscoped waivers apply would refuse (I1-I6).
threats.mitigation: Every import waiver record folds through the same classifier as apply: a record apply would refuse is refused, listed in problems[] with its line and the reason, and import exits non-zero; an unresolvable --ref never yields a stored document-wide waiver.

threats.title: Migrating a legacy document through import silently loses its reviewed waivers
threats.statement: Once import refuses unscoped and single-ref waivers (T9), an honest author re-importing a v4 stream (or migrating for the format bump, D3) loses every waiver the stream carries, scoped-in-intent ones (I2, I6) included, and the scoped form apply accepts is itself rejected as unexpected keys (scoped-record.txt).
threats.mitigation: Every waiver import refuses is named in the import envelope with its line, code and scope, together with its replacement: a scoped refs+contentHash waive op the fold accepts for a scoped code, or the rewrite remedy for a never code; a record in the refs+contentHash form apply accepts is not rejected for its keys.

threats.title: Hand-edited JSON waivers skip the fold (risk R4: a fence with no check-time twin)
threats.statement: The agent writes waivers[] directly: code-only (hand-never-code-only), requirementId with a hash (hand-ref-with-hash, which bindsCurrentText accepts today), requirementIds with no hash (hand-refs-no-hash), both requirementId and requirementIds, an empty requirementIds, requirement keys instead of UUIDs, or a never code with a hash it computed itself. None of these passes a fold, and at base compat forwards every one with no hash, and the engine applies it.
threats.mitigation: A stored waiver reaches the engine exactly when the S3 fold would accept the same waiver as an op on the same document (refs equal to a finding's ids, contentHash matching the current text, scoped-class code); every other stored shape is inert and disclosed as waiver-inert.
threats.evidenceFloor: check-time twin over the raw channel

threats.title: A waived blocking lint re-admits a requirement and lets the run verify
threats.statement: A scoped, hash-bound waiver of GTWR_R7_VAGUE (wording, scoped, so S3 accepts it) re-admits ORD-R1 to the solver (W1c, isWaivedBlocking). The requirement is decided only because of the waiver, and an agent can waive every blocking lint it meets until the run verifies (blocking-lint-one, blocking-lint-both, the gaming fixture waived-blocking-lint).
threats.mitigation: Every requirement re-admitted by a waived blocking lint is named in a waived-blocking-lint demotion, verified is false, and --strict exits 3; with no stored waivers the demotions equal base's.

threats.title: The waived-blocking-lint set is computed from different waivers than the engine applied
threats.statement: The plan computes the demotion at the app boundary as excludedIds(gateRequirements(reqs, [])) minus the post-waiver excluded set. If the post-waiver set is computed from a narrower waiver list than the one toEngineDoc handed the engine (or from the raw document while the engine got more, through a twin bug), a requirement the engine re-admitted is missing from the demotion.
threats.mitigation: The waived-blocking-lint ids equal the requirements excluded with no waivers minus those excluded under exactly the waiver list the engine received from toEngineDoc; adding or removing an inert or stale waiver leaves the demotion unchanged.

threats.title: repair.ops teach a waive for a never code, or a waive shape the S3 fold refuses
threats.statement: Agents pipe repair.ops into apply. At base repair.ts offers scopedWaive ops for FND_RELATIONAL_UNCHECKED, FND_NUMERIC_UNCOMPARED and FND_NUMBER_SPELLING_CANDIDATE (disclosure and triage, never), the opposition and SIMILAR_SEMANTIC waiver through fromFindingMessage, and a single-`ref` waive of the blocking code for excluded-from-formal, which the S3 fold refuses. The advice either teaches the forbidden move or a dead one.
threats.mitigation: Over every report-corpus and fixture document, every op in every repair.ops decodes as a DocumentOp and the S3 fold accepts it on the checked document, and no offered waive op names a never-class code.

threats.title: Engine demotion actions and finding suggestions say 'waive' for never codes
threats.statement: Engine prose tells the agent to waive: check.ts demotion actions (the 'or waive it' site and others), semantic.ts (~:569 'declare them distinct with the repair waiver', ~:954 'waive this finding'), numeric-contradiction.ts (six sites), number-spelling.ts, quantity-alias.ts, and engine codes.ts descriptions. The report corpus omits messages and suggestions, so no committed guard reads them.
threats.mitigation: No demotion action, finding message or suggestion emitted for a never-class code contains 'waive', checked over the report corpus and the fixture documents (the guard reads the prose fields the corpus row omits).

threats.title: The installed skill body, scope prose and explain keep teaching the waive move
threats.statement: craft.ts (the installed skill body) says 'the always-safe third option is the reviewed waiver' for FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE, a never code; scope.ts coverageDemotion says a requirement can be 'covered or waived'; explain and the catalog rows render the same corpus. An agent that installed the skill follows it regardless of what the fold does.
threats.mitigation: The skill body, scope prose, explain output and AGENTS.md offer no waive remedy for any never-class code: 'or waived' is absent from scope, and the skill body's opposition-candidate guidance names no waiver; check:agents shows no drift.

threats.title: The published statement claims enforcement that one channel lacks
threats.statement: Flipping WAIVABILITY_ENFORCED to true makes every surface say '`waive` refuses a never code, and `check` ignores a stored waiver on one'. If only apply enforces it while import or the stored-document path does not, the published guarantee is false and a reader trusts verified: true over a waived never finding.
threats.mitigation: WAIVABILITY_ENFORCED is true only when, for one never code of each never class, apply refuses it, import refuses it, and check ignores it in a stored document; the 'NOT enforced' sentence is absent from every surface.
threats.evidenceFloor: check-time twin over the raw channel

threats.title: Replacement ops name commands or verbs this build does not have
threats.statement: The plan's replacement for a never-code waiver is `vocab distinct` or `propose-vocabulary --rescope-waivers`; ops.ts has no vocab verb, the flag is not in the story, and the CLI `waive` has no --refs. A waiver-inert diagnostic that offers them leaves the author with a reviewed waiver gone and a remedy that fails (legacy-mixed W3, repro-scoped).
threats.mitigation: Every replacement op on a waiver-inert or ignoredWaivers entry decodes as a DocumentOp and folds under MUTATE_OPTIONS on the checked document, every replacement command parses under this build's CLI, and a never-code entry with no such op says 'rewrite required' and offers no waive.

threats.title: Replacement waive ops launder an unreviewed legacy waiver into the reviewed form
threats.statement: For a code-only legacy waiver of a scoped code (legacy-mixed W1), waiver-inert offers one scoped refs+contentHash waive per finding it matches today. Applied mechanically with the legacy reason, these turn a waiver nobody reviewed per finding into the exact-set, hash-bound form that reads as 'reviewed over this text'; the same holds for the '<why this finding does not apply>' placeholder reason repair ops carry, which the fold accepts unedited.
threats.mitigation: A replacement waive op carries a placeholder reason, never the legacy waiver's reason, and covers only findings the inert waiver matches on the current text; whether the fold refuses a reason that still holds the placeholder is put to a person.

threats.title: The gaming harness does not measure the raw channel or a scoped never-code waive
threats.statement: Every harness move goes through the fold (Edit kinds ops, reparse, run). After S3 the 11 waive-by-code rows close because the fold refuses the code-only stream, and that refusal is the same whether the fold checks the class or only the scope, so the harness cannot tell T1 from T3 closed. Nothing writes a stored waiver into the JSON, so T8 and T11 (R4) are unmeasured, and a missing check-time twin is a live escape the exactness test cannot see.
threats.mitigation: The harness measures (a) a scoped waive of each baseline finding over its exact ids and current hash and (b) the same waivers and a code-only one written into the stored document with no fold, and on every fixture whose seeded finding is never-class neither reaches a clean verdict.
threats.evidenceFloor: check-time twin over the raw channel

threats.title: KNOWN_ESCAPES rows or the waive move are deleted to match the change rather than closed by it
threats.statement: The builder deletes the 11 waive-by-code rows, or the waive-by-code move itself, or regenerates the shard and report-corpus snapshots, so the exactness test passes whether or not the escapes stopped. With the move gone, OP_COVERAGE maps the waive verb to nothing that measures it.
threats.mitigation: The 11 waive-by-code rows are deleted with the move still registered and the exactness test green over every shard; re-adding any one of them turns the test red; OP_COVERAGE maps waive to at least one move that emits a waive op; every changed report-corpus row is a verdict delta attributable to AC-5-6.

threats.title: A finding code with no FINDING_CLASS row falls into a default class
threats.statement: findingClassOf returns undefined for a code outside FindingKey; the plan adds vocabulary-codes.ts, intent-codes.ts and delta-codes.ts, unioned by catalog.ts. A classifier that treats undefined as waivable lets a waiver of a new verdict or anchor code through both fences. `code in FINDING_CLASS` is also true for inherited names (constructor, toString), and any 'GTWR_' string is scoped, so an invented code takes a class nobody decided.
threats.mitigation: A code findingClassOf does not classify by an own row is refused at write time with ERR_WAIVER_REFUSED and inert at check (hand-unknown-code); every code the catalog publishes has its own FINDING_CLASS row, so adding a code without one fails the gate.

threats.title: Case or whitespace variants of a code string slip between the classifier and the matcher
threats.statement: The fold trims the code; the engine, the gate and unwaive compare exactly; the classifier looks up the exact string. A hand-edited ' FND_CONTRADICTION' or 'fnd_contradiction' is unknown to the classifier; if the twin normalizes differently from the matcher, or a later edit makes the match case-insensitive, a never code passes as unknown and suppresses. A padded stored code also cannot be removed by the unwaive op a replacement offers.
threats.mitigation: The classifier, the check-time twin and the engine match read one normalized code: every case and whitespace variant of every never-class code is refused at write time, is inert at check, and suppresses no finding.

threats.title: A content hash binds text, not a reviewer: any writer can mint a qualifying scoped waiver
threats.statement: requirementsContentHash is public: check prints it in repair.ops and an agent can compute it. So a refs+hash waiver of a scoped code proves only that the waiver names this text, not that anyone reviewed it. After S3 this is the only waiver that applies, and an agent can mint one for every wording and structural finding (FND_CYCLE on derives-cycle verifies by design once scoped).
threats.mitigation: Every waiver the engine applied is listed in the check payload with its code, requirement ids and reason, and the published scope says a content hash binds the text and not the reviewer; a person decides whether the scoped FND_CYCLE escape on derives-cycle is listed as a designed escape.

threats.title: Closing the waive path displaces the agent onto other clean moves
threats.statement: With waivers refused and waived-blocking-lint demoting, the shortest path to green becomes deleting one side of the conflict (delete-requirement@first/@second on waived-blocking-lint, already KNOWN_ESCAPES under AC-5-2) or a run knob. S3 must not open a new clean pair while closing the waive rows.
threats.mitigation: After S3 the set of clean (fixture, move) pairs over every shard is base's minus the 11 waive-by-code rows, with no pair added.

threats.title: An engine logic edit weakens the existing pair-bound decline
threats.statement: S3 may edit engine prose only. Moving the waiver rules into compat invites deleting PAIR_BOUND_CODES or the textBound test in isWaived as 'now redundant'; if the compat twin then has a gap (T11), the engine no longer catches a code-only FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE waiver in a stored document.
threats.mitigation: The engine tier's diff in S3 is prose only: waiver-scope.test.ts, verified.test.ts and package-boundary.test.ts pass unchanged, and a stored code-only FND_OPPOSITION_CANDIDATE waiver is declined even when compat forwards it.

assumptions.text: CI runs `pnpm check` on a fresh clone, and symspec.config.json is CODEOWNED, so the gate's own invocation is outside the agent's reach (D5, D8, R6).
requirementsContentHash is collision-resistant over meaningOf(requirement); a waiver cannot be bound to two different texts.
The report corpus and the gaming fixtures together exercise every advice site that can emit a waive op or the word 'waive' for a never code; a site neither reaches is unguarded (T14, T15).

coverage.uncoveredNote: release has no threat in this model: the version bump and feat! marker move no certificate; the reviewed-waiver loss a breaking release causes is T6, T8, T10 and T18.
